properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 1:39AM EDT until October 11 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...
West Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 400 AM EDT.

* At 139 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain have fallen over the past 12
hours. Steady rises are occurring in area streams including the
Linville River, Wilson Creek, Johns River, Mulberry Creek and
Warrior Fork Creek. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Crossnore, Table Rock, B.R. Parkway-Linville Falls To Grandfather,
Linville Falls, B.R. Parkway-Little Switzerland To Linville, Lake
James State Park, Grandfather Mountain State Park, Lake James,
Jonas Ridge and Edgemont.

Wilson Creek at Adako Rd, 3 miles southwest of Colletsville has risen
above flood stage and is still rising. Flooding of low-lying areas
adjacent to Wilson Creek is developing with lesser impacts to
vulnerable property.  More significant floodwaters are beginning to
impact low-lying areas, with inundation approximately 2-4 ft deep.
Low-water crossings may be inundated with up to 2-3 ft of
floodwaters.  Campgrounds, secondary roads, and outbuildings may be
experiencing flooding up to 1-2 ft deep.  Flooding less than 1 ft
deep may begin impacting basements and primary roads.
properties.instruction:
Only when it is safe to do so, please report flooding or landslides
threatening roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling 1...800...2 6 7...8 1 0 1, by
posting on our Facebook page, or by posting on X using hashtag
NWSGSP. Your message should describe the specific location, address,
or intersection where impacts occurred and the depth of flooding
observed.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Burke County in western North Carolina...

* Until 615 AM EDT.

* At 1224 AM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady
rainfall produced 3-6 inches across Burke County, saturating area
soils.  Doppler radar shows several rounds of torrential rainfall
have moved through the area from the south, capable of producing
1.5-3 inches of rainfall on top of saturated soils.  This rainfall
will cause new areas of Minor flooding to develop.

* Areas of greatest concern include along Hunting Creek near
Morganton; poorly draining areas of Morganton and other urban areas
along US 70; Silver Creek south of Glen Alpine; and Henry and Jacob
forks of the South Fork Catawba River near South Mountains State
Park.

* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the
next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.  Only 12 inches
of water can strand your vehicle or sweep it away.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...

properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Rutherford County in western North Carolina...

* Until 445 AM EDT Sunday.

* At 1039 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen, with additional torrential rainfall moving into the
warned area. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly. Rapid rises should be expected on area creeks and
streams, including along Cleghorn Creek in Rutherfordton, Floyds
Creek near Forest City, and Mountain Creek near Green Hill.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Forest City, Rutherfordton, Spindale, Ellenboro, Bostic, South
Mountains State Park, Alexander Mills, Sunshine, Union Mills and
Caroleen.

Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms will develop over the
next few hours and the threat will persist through the early morning
hours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very efficient at
producing heavy rainfall.  Flash flooding is imminent or occurring
across the area. Caution is advised near any stream or other
vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain
develops. Please have a plan in place should you experience flash
flooding and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation
orders from Emergency Management officials.

flooding; Nix Creek near Providence; Crooked Creek near Moffitt
Hill; and the Upper Catawba River between Old Fort and Pleasant
Gardens, including along Lytle Mountain Rd, where a foot of flood
waters have currently closed the roadway.  Additionally, a
landslide has been observed on NC-226A with minor impacts to the
roadway.  Additional areas of Minor flooding are expected to
develop over the next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and
heed all evacuation orders from local Emergency Management
officials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-
access areas, and campgrounds.  Low-lying roadways are
likely to be flooded.  An isolated landslide or two cannot
be ruled out.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Marion, Old Fort, Lake James, Lake James State Park, B.R.
Parkway-Craggy To Little Switzerland, B.R. Parkway-Little
Switzerland To Linville, Linville Falls, Pleasant Gardens, Sugar
Hill and Glenwood.

8-8.5 feet before slowing or cresting.  High flows along the Rocky
Broad River into Chimney Rock will result in flooding of US 64/74

are expected to develop over the next 1-2 hours.  Please obey all
barricades and heed all evacuation orders from local Emergency
Management officials.

access areas, and  campgrounds.  Low-lying roadways are
likely to be flooded.  An  isolated landslide or two
cannot be ruled out.
